correctness.rationale: For identical unit chores, ex-ante weighted envy-free is exactly E[X_i]=m w_i and deterministic WEF1 is (x_i-1)/w_i <= x_j/w_j for nonempty recipients. For m<n a missing recipient forces all counts <=1, yielding hypersimplex membership; m=n forces counts one. At m=n+1 only an extra chore can be assigned to a maximal-weight recipient; mixing over S produces (t+1)/(t(n+1)) vs 1/(n+1). Exchange-chain inequalities between supported vectors give rational ratios along edges and component total weights N_C/m, hence each support set determines at most one rational weight. n=2 the interval (m-1)p <= x <= (m-1)p+1 yields mp integer or (m-1)p integer. These proof implications are sound. A separately written Fraction enumeration checked 440 two-agent configurations; bounded tests do not prove general claims.
